claims.text: A logical shift moves every bit one or more places left or right: the bits shifted out at the end are lost, and zeros enter at the other end.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A logical left shift by one place doubles an unsigned value's bits each place moved, and a logical right shift by one place halves it, discarding the remainder.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A cyclic shift moves the bits that fall off one end round to the other end, so no bits are lost.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An arithmetic shift keeps the sign bit: on a right shift the sign bit is copied into the vacated positions, so a negative value stays negative.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A bit mask is a pattern of bits, with 1s in the positions of interest and 0s elsewhere, that is combined with a value to test, set or clear the chosen bits.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: AND with a mask tests: the 1s in the mask keep the value's own bits and the 0s clear the rest, so the result shows what the chosen bits held.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: OR with a mask sets: the 1s in the mask force those bits to 1 whatever they held, and the 0s leave the value's bits unchanged, so the chosen lines are switched on.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
